Recall that if  $A=UΣ{V}^{T}$ is a singular value decomposition of a $3\times 2$ matrix $A,$ then

- $Σ$ is a $3\times 2$ matrix with nonnegative elements on the main diagonal and zeroes outside the main diagonal,

- $U$ is an orthogonal $3\times 3$ matrix,

- $V$ is an orthogonal $2\times 2$ matrix.

From the matrix $Σ,$ we deduce that ${\sigma }_{1}=6$ and ${\sigma }_{2}=4.$
Also, the columns ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{2}$ of $V$ give us the right singular vectors of $A.$

Therefore, we can compute the $1$st and $2$nd columns of $U$ as follows:

- First, we compute ${u}_{1}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{u}_{1} & =\frac{1}{{\sigma }_{1}}A{v}_{1} \\  & =\frac{1}{6}[\begin{aligned}0 & 4 \\ 4 & 2 \\ 4 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{\sqrt{5}} \\ \frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{6}[\begin{aligned}\frac{4}{\sqrt{5}} \\ \frac{10}{\sqrt{5}} \\ \frac{8}{\sqrt{5}}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{3\sqrt{5}} \\ \frac{5}{3\sqrt{5}} \\ \frac{4}{3\sqrt{5}}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

- Then, we compute ${u}_{2}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{u}_{2} & =\frac{1}{{\sigma }_{2}}A{v}_{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{4}[\begin{aligned}0 & 4 \\ 4 & 2 \\ 4 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}} \\ \frac{2}{\sqrt{5}}\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{4}[\begin{aligned}\frac{8}{\sqrt{5}} \\ 0 \\ -\frac{4}{\sqrt{5}}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{\sqrt{5}} \\ 0 \\ -\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Since we do not have the third singular value, we can't use the same formula to find the third column of $U.$ But we know that $U$ must be orthogonal. Hence, we must find a vector 

$$
{u}_{3}=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}]
$$

such that 

$$
{\begin{aligned}{u}_{1}\cdot {u}_{3}=0 \\ {u}_{2}\cdot {u}_{3}=0,\end{aligned}\,‖{u}_{3}‖=1.
$$

Solving this system, which is equivalent to

$$
{\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{3\sqrt{5}}{x}_{1}+\frac{5}{3\sqrt{5}}{x}_{2}+\frac{4}{3\sqrt{5}}{x}_{3}=0 \\ \frac{2}{\sqrt{5}}{x}_{1}-\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}{x}_{3}=0\end{aligned}\,⟹\,{\begin{aligned}2{x}_{1}+5{x}_{2}+4{x}_{3}=0 \\ 2{x}_{1}-{x}_{3}=0,\end{aligned}
$$

we get the nonzero normalized solution 

$$
{u}_{3}=[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{3} \\ -\frac{2}{3} \\ \frac{2}{3}\end{aligned}].
$$

Finally, we construct the matrix $U:$

$$
U=[\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{3\sqrt{5}} & \frac{2}{\sqrt{5}} & \frac{1}{3} \\ \frac{5}{3\sqrt{5}} & 0 & -\frac{2}{3} \\ \frac{4}{3\sqrt{5}} & -\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}} & \frac{2}{3}\end{aligned}]
$$
